notes: Three metrics moved far beyond tolerance and all three are consequences of construction working. referenceLivingMages and referenceLibraryDepth rise because universities the god funds now get finished by laborers, so they open seats, seats take students, students become mages, and mages fill libraries. mc-harness recorded the old behaviour as 'universities-are-founded-and-never-finished' and that entry is annotated on this branch rather than deleted. referencePeakPopulation falling is the other side of the same change and is the number most worth an author's attention: carrying capacity's provisioning multiplier now reads the food stock alone rather than every material summed, and laborers standing on a building site produce nothing that month. Both are documented decisions, neither is tuned, and if the intended world is one where a god may not halve its own peak population by over-founding then the lever is a cap on the divertible labour share, which this branch deliberately did not invent. perRunTimeoutMs was also raised from 600000 to 1800000: one archivist run now takes 305 s alone, measured with reproduce-run.mjs, against a cap sized for a build whose universities never completed, and pool.ts says that budget is sized against what the simulation does.

The universe these numbers describe is still degenerate, and the changes folded into this file moved which ways rather than removing them. Two items leave the list: library depth is no longer pinned near two distinct nodes, because scribing survives now that parchment and bread are different things; and universities the god funds now actually get finished, so completedUniversities is no longer identically one. What remains degenerate: the god is still passive in the two fast gates, so 400 of the 432 runs measure the simulation's own evolution and not play; ascension eligibility still opens by passive accumulation, so the ascension rate remains a statement about a clock; the scribable list is still cost-ordered, so the same cheap nodes are copied repeatedly; and several observation channels still saturate. Read every figure here as a vital sign of a build, not as a description of the finished game.
rationale: Merge of origin/main into w29/city-and-supply-chain (PR #42), and the baselines are regenerated because both parents are invalid against this tree. Provenance first: this tree loads contentRevision 2c67315ae04ee6c74dfa204474af4eb6 and the superseded baseline was recorded at d37624e36be00f59cf21b87ff6eba144, so its numbers describe a different build and a delta against them is a category error rather than a regression. Two movements meet here and only one of them is in the delta below. W17's value-sensitive acquirer (contracts.md 2.11) is the movement the superseded baseline describes -- and this branch already contained it, which is why autonomy-weight.json merged add/add byte-identically and why referenceNodesKnown at five years reads 29.46 here against main's 29.44 and the pre-acquirer 22.115. What this branch carries that main lacks is the whole of the delta, and it is three landed changes rather than one: W6's five ascension constants, W8's raid-engagement constants, and this branch's own economy wire -- the single materials scalar became three kinds (food, stone, vellum), and knowledge reached the economy for the first time, every baseline in this repository before it having been recorded against a build in which resourceYieldBonuses was a hardcoded empty array and advanceConstruction had no caller outside its own tests, so both economy primitives were unreachable by any path. The merge's own finding, worth recording because it is what a reader will want to check: this tree reproduces the branch's committed figures exactly, metric for metric, in all three gates, so main's 104 commits since the merge base moved nothing any of these sweeps can see and there is no acquirer-by-economy interaction to report. These numbers are a measurement of what this build did on this date and NOT a balance claim: release-plan.md forbids one before 0.5.0, every magnitude the change introduced is marked untuned, and nothing here has been tuned against a target. This gate's superseded baseline is invalid on two counts rather than one: besides the contentRevision above, the sweep configuration hashes to 268779c4 against the recorded da7ead15, because this branch raised perRunTimeoutMs from 600000 to 1800000 for the reason the note below gives. Measured against it over 32 runs at 2400 ticks: referenceLivingMages 70.406 -> 461.031 (94.51 SE), referencePeakPopulation 19603 -> 29489 (34.59 SE), referencePopulation 6116.84 -> 16231.78 (7.48 SE) and referencePopulationChange the same, referenceGrimoires 110.125 -> 255.406 (4.10 SE) and referenceKnowledgeInstances 1942.13 -> 3100.31 (3.43 SE); referenceLibraryDepth 24.938 -> 31.094 (1.83 SE), referenceNodesKnown 65.469 -> 67.063 (0.12 SE), referenceNodesGained the same and referenceNodesGainedFinalQuarter 2.063 -> 2.469 (0.35 SE) are all inside tolerance. Those figures compare two builds that differ by three landed changes, so read them beside the branch's own lineage, where the economy wire alone moved referenceLivingMages 105.5 -> 461.0 (18.20 SE), referenceLibraryDepth 9.94 -> 31.09 (6.50 SE) and referencePeakPopulation 50080 -> 29489 (-156 SE). The peak-population direction is opposite in the two comparisons and neither is a contradiction: against this branch's own ancestor the economy wire halves the peak, and against main it raises it, because main's ancestor is a build without W6's or W8's constants and reached a different peak to begin with.
